newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to OK China routes, direct sailings soon.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to OK China routes, direct sailings soon.

text.p: Taiwan's transport ministry said on Thursday it would approve direct Taiwan-China sailings by mainland vessels that submit applications and that such crossings could begin as early as 10 days from now.

"The (Taiwan) ministry is able to approve the five mainland shippers for across-strait links within a week of receiving them," said Ting Chan-neng, head of the ministry's navigation and aviation section.
Ting was referring to five mainland shipping companies that received approval on Wednesday from China's communist government to make cross-straits passages.

Ting said the mainland shippers still had to apply to Taiwan's transport ministry before the crossings could take place, but said approval would be granted swiftly after receipt of their official documentation and applications.

With both governments' tacit approval, shipping companies from Taiwan and China reached an agreement in February that would loosen Taipei's 48-year-old ban on direct crossings of the Taiwan strait, although many conditions would apply.
The crossings would link only the southern Taiwan port of Kaohsiung and the closest mainland port, Xiamen, a special economic zone in southeastern Fujian province.

Taiwan has said Kaohsiung was ready to receive ships sailing directly from China as long as they are owned by mainland, Taiwan or Hong Kong interests and fly the flag of Hong Kong or a third country -- not communist China's red five-star.
Taipei does not regard the new service as a "direct shipping link" but rather an "offshore transshipment" scheme because mainland cargoes will not be allowed to enter Taiwan customs.
Rather, they can be processed in an "offshore" bonded zone in Kaohsiung outside of customs for onward shipment.
Taipei's conditions seek to ensure the breakthrough does not undermine the sovereignty of the island's exiled Republic of China, which does not recognise the communists' sovereignty.
Beijing's Ministry of Communications on Wednesday approved five mainland firms for direct service.
They are Fujian Provincial Shipping Co Ltd, Xiamen Shipping Co Ltd, Mawei Shipping Co Ltd, Fujian Foreign Trade Centre Shipping Co Ltd and major national line China Ocean Shipping.
About a dozen Taiwan shippers have been approved by Taipei for cross-straits shipping and have applied to Beijing, which has said it was processing their paperwork.

Industry analysts expect Taiwan's Yangming Marine Transport Corp, Uniglory Marine, Wan Hai Lines, and Chinese Maritime Transport Ltd would be the first group of Taiwan's shippers to participate the link.

Taiwan has banned direct links since 1949, when it was split from the newly communist mainland by a civil war, though cross-strait trade and investment -- most of it routed "indirectly" via Hong Kong -- has flourished since a political thaw began in the late 1980s.
